one_liner: Small MIT C 2D vector library with a Cairo-like canvas API; no published speed comparison against Cairo, Skia or Blend2D.
what_it_does: A standalone C11 software renderer that draws paths (fill, stroke, dash), solid, linear/radial gradient and image paints, text from TrueType fonts, clips and Porter-Duff compositing into a 32-bit premultiplied ARGB surface, and can read and write PNG/JPG. The API is a Cairo-style immediate-mode canvas (save/restore, move_to/arc, set_rgb, fill_preserve, stroke) rather than a source-compatible Cairo replacement. It is the rasteriser behind LunaSVG and PlutoSVG.
how_it_is_fast: Nothing in the repository claims or measures speed; the design is simply lean. Coverage comes from a vendored copy of FreeType's ftgrays cell/area scanline rasteriser (8-bit anti-aliased spans, 8 KB stack pool with band splitting) and FreeType's stroker, clipping is done by intersecting span lists, and compositing uses Qt-style SWAR pixel arithmetic (BYTE_MUL, INTERPOLATE_PIXEL_255 on two channels per 32-bit word) with 1024-entry gradient lookup tables. The only SIMD is an SSE2 memfill for opaque solid spans; there is no JIT, tiling, sparse-strip or multithreaded pipeline of the kind Blend2D or Vello CPU use.
when_to_use: You need a dependency-free C library (vendored stb_truetype, stb_image, stb_image_write) to draw anti-aliased paths, gradients and text into an ARGB32 buffer, for example on embedded, homebrew or game targets.
You want Cairo-like drawing semantics without pulling in Cairo, pixman, FreeType and fontconfig, and footprint matters more than peak throughput.
You already render SVG with LunaSVG or PlutoSVG and want direct access to the same backend.
MIT licensing with a small codebase (about a dozen C files) that is easy to audit or vendor.
when_not_to_use: You need proven speed over Cairo or Skia: no benchmark exists, and VGCPU-Benchmark wires up a plutovg backend (labelled 0.0.4) but commits no results.

Throughput-critical rendering of large or complex scenes: compositing is scalar apart from an SSE2 fill and rendering is single-threaded; Blend2D, Vello CPU and ThorVG are the measured options in this catalog.
You need separable blend modes (multiply, screen, overlay and so on): only the 12 Porter-Duff operators exist.
Real text layout: glyphs come from stb_truetype outlines with no shaping, kerning or hinting.
Pixel formats other than premultiplied ARGB32 (RGB565 and similar were requested in issues #33 and #41).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (Meson or CMake), or source-drop of the source/ directory
integration.dependencies: libm; optional C11 threads.h or pthreads for font-cache locks; stb_truetype, stb_image and stb_image_write are vendored
integration.min_toolchain: C11 compiler (Meson default gnu11; CMake C_STANDARD 11); Meson 1.0+ or CMake 3.15+
integration.platforms: Portable C; CI builds on Linux, macOS and Windows; SSE2 path only for memfill, scalar elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: Canvas and surface objects are not synchronised (one thread per canvas). Reference counts are atomic (C11 stdatomic or Interlocked). Font faces and the font-face cache lock a mutex, but that mutex compiles to a no-op when neither Win32 nor C11 threads.h is available.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: Cairo-like concepts and the same premultiplied ARGB32 layout as CAIRO_FORMAT_ARGB32, but a different API (plutovg_canvas_*), no PDF/SVG/PS backends and no blend modes beyond Porter-Duff

gotchas: Transformed non-tiled images are sampled nearest-neighbour (blend_transformed_argb); bilinear sampling exists only for tiled textures under rotation or shear, and PR #72 to extend it is still open.
Strokes are built after the transform with one width scaled by hypot(sx, sy)/sqrt(2), so non-uniform scale or skew gives a uniform-width stroke instead of the elliptical pen Cairo produces.

If a single scanline needs more cells than the 8 KB stack pool, PVG_FT_Raster_Render restarts the whole path with a doubled heap pool (up to 8 MB), skipping spans already emitted; beyond 8 MB the path is silently left partly drawn, since the call returns void.
Vendored FreeType-derived files (plutovg-ft-raster.c, plutovg-ft-stroker.c, plutovg-ft-math.c) carry the FreeType Project License, which asks for credit in documentation; the rest is MIT.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Blend2D, ThorVG or tiny-skia when a small, dependency-free C library with a Cairo-like API matters more than measured speed; for throughput Blend2D (and Vello CPU) have independent numbers beating Skia and Cairo, while plutovg has none.
verified_claims_summary: No speed claim exists to verify: the README, release notes and issue tracker carry no numbers, and the only independent suite that includes plutovg (mfabbri77/VGCPU-Benchmark, with Cairo 1.18.2, Skia m124 and Blend2D) commits its harness but no results.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-07-16, v1.3.3 released 2026-05-18; May 2026 fixes for allocation-failure handling and surface-size overflow); MIT plus FreeType-licensed rasteriser files, so usability is mixed but practical to vendor.
